changes.after: A temporary file gives a task its own file that can be removed when the task ends.

before:
require "tempfile" loads the available library. Tempfile.create with a block creates a uniquely named temporary file and closes and removes it on block exit; do not construct predictable global temporary filenames yourself.

The array ["study", ".txt"] passed to Tempfile.create supplies a filename prefix and suffix. The block receives the open temporary file object; its generated name is not a stable value to assert.

File.basename extracts the final path component; File.join assembles components but does not prevent traversal or authorize a user-supplied path. rewind resets the file position to the beginning before read; otherwise reading immediately after writing would start at the end. end_with? tests a string suffix. The generated temporary path stays local here and is not printed.

File.exist?(path) receives a path and returns true when that path exists, otherwise false. The final call below therefore checks removal after the temporary-file block, rather than merely checking whether the handle is closed.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
require "tempfile"
saved_path = nil
Tempfile.create(["study", ".txt"]) do |file|
  saved_path = file.path
  file.write("ok")
  file.rewind
  puts file.read
  puts File.basename(file.path).end_with?(".txt")
end
puts File.exist?(saved_path)

```

Expected output or behavior: ok
true
false. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain why File.join is not a path-traversal defense. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A temporary file gives a task its own file that can be removed when the task ends.
Here Ruby closes and removes the temporary file when the block finishes.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
require "tempfile"
saved_path = nil
Tempfile.create(["study", ".txt"]) do |file|
  saved_path = file.path
  file.write("ok")
  file.rewind
  puts file.read
  puts File.basename(file.path).end_with?(".txt")
end
puts File.exist?(saved_path)
```
The output is `ok`, then `true`, then `false`. Inside the block the file can be read and its name ends in .txt. After the block its saved path no longer exists.
Change the requested ending to .log but keep the .txt check.
